guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — statin use for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease
guideline.section: Adults 40–75 with ≥ 1 CVD risk factor (dyslipidaemia, diabetes, hypertension or smoking) and an estimated 10-year CVD risk ≥ 10%: prescribe a statin (grade B); requires lipid measurement and a 10-year risk estimate
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Statin use for the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease in adults: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2022;328:746–753.

guideline.name: 2019 ACC/AHA guideline on the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease
guideline.section: Adults 40–75: estimate 10-year ASCVD risk (pooled cohort equations) to guide statin therapy; assess and treat tobacco use at every visit
guideline.citation: Arnett DK, Blumenthal RS, Albert MA, et al. 2019 ACC/AHA guideline on the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease. Circulation. 2019;140:e596–e646.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for lung cancer
guideline.section: Annual low-dose CT for adults 50–80 with a ≥ 20 pack-year history who currently smoke or quit within the past 15 years (grade B)
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for lung cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2021;325:962–970.

rationale: Statin decisions in primary prevention depend on a lipid profile and a 10-year risk estimate; smoking cessation is the single most effective intervention for this patient.
